beats.beat: The company manufactures and sells specialty chemicals under four categories: Functional Additives, Chemically Modified Minerals, Soft Minerals, and Hard Minerals. These products are used across industries such as paints, plastics, cosmetics, and construction.

It has a long-term arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, to market and sell its products through the promoter's network. This creates a key dependency; the filing lists 'support of our holding company' as a competitive strength.
Top 10 customers accounted for about 59% of revenue in each of the last three fiscal years (FY2015–2017), indicating concentrated customer dependence.
The company exports to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, and Sri Lanka, with cumulative exports of ₹1068.18 lakh over five years.
Other strengths cited: diversified product portfolio, import substitution potential, continuous R&D, and a strong management team.

beats.beat: The company reported a profit after tax turning positive from FY2015 onwards. PAT was -₹0.27 crore in FY2013, -₹0.12 crore in FY2014, ₹1.50 crore in FY2015, ₹0.90 crore in FY2016, ₹1.75 crore in FY2017, and ₹1.33 crore for the six months ended September 30, 2017.
Operating cash flows have been volatile: ₹2.01 crore in FY2013, ₹1.28 crore in FY2014, ₹4.22 crore in FY2015, ₹8.03 crore in FY2016, -₹3.50 crore in FY2017, and ₹1.25 crore in H1 FY2018.
Total assets as at March 31, 2017 stood at ₹32.74 crore, compared to ₹30.19 crore as at September 30, 2017.
Basic earnings per share (EPS) improved from -₹0.45 in FY2013 to ₹2.43 in FY2017. For the six months ended September 30, 2017, EPS was ₹1.48.
Revenue from operations is not explicitly disclosed in the provided DRHP excerpts, limiting a full revenue trend analysis.

beats.beat: The promoters are Mr. Chandresh S. Parikh, Mr. Atil C. Parikh, Mr. Rajesh C. Parikh, and 20 Microns Limited (corporate promoter). They collectively hold 89,48,270 equity shares, representing 99.76% of the pre-issue paid-up capital.
Promoter group members (excluding promoters) hold an additional 21,510 shares, or 0.24% of the pre-issue capital.
The company has entered into related party transactions with its promoter group, which may continue in the future. Full details are referenced in the financial statements.

The company does not own the premises for its manufacturing facilities at Waghodia (Plot 347) and Tirunelveli, nor its administrative offices in Bhuj and Udaipur, creating reliance on leased properties.

Past instances of non-filing or delayed filing with the Registrar of Companies have occurred, and certain statutory licenses for the manufacturing facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia have not yet been obtained.
The company has contingent liabilities of ₹29.11 lakh as of September 30, 2017, as per the restated financial statements.

beats.beat: The Indian specialty chemicals market (excluding agrochemicals and dyestuff) was estimated at about ₹1,000 billion in FY2017, part of the larger chemicals industry of ₹5,800–6,200 billion.

CRISIL Research estimates the specialty chemicals segment grew at 10–12% CAGR from FY2014 to FY2017 and is expected to grow at 12–14% CAGR going forward, driven by end-use demand, urbanization, and government initiatives.
The industry is highly fragmented, with SMEs holding 70–75% market share, but global players compete on product development. Only a few Indian players have the scale to match global giants.
Key growth drivers include increased consumption, rising GDP (7.1% in FY2017), urban population growth (31% in 2011, expected 36% by 2020), and 100% FDI allowed in the sector.
The filing notes that India's chemicals industry imports more than it exports, with imports growing at 6.4% CAGR vs exports at 6% CAGR between 2012–13 and 2016–17.
Regulatory aspects: GST implemented July 1, 2017; Draft National Chemical Policy aims to increase chemicals' GDP share; REACH regulations govern exports to Europe.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals Limited processes and sells specialty chemicals — Functional Additives, Chemically Modified Minerals, Soft Minerals and Hard Minerals — and relies on its corporate promoter 20 Microns Limited for marketing and distribution.
The company is raising funds through a fresh issue to set up a new manufacturing facility in Waghodia, Gujarat, and to list on the SME platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE).
Its promoters — the Parikh family and 20 Microns Limited — hold 99.76% of the pre-issue equity, making this a tightly held firm opening up to public investors for the first time.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who 20 Microns Nano Minerals is, what it does (specialty chemicals processing and selling), that it is raising capital for a new facility and listing on NSE EMERGE, and that the filing reveals heavy promoter dependence and mixed cash flows.

beats.beat: The IPO is a fresh issue of equity shares; the exact offer size is not disclosed in the DRHP excerpt. The lead manager is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited, and the registrar is Link Intime India Private Limited.
Proceeds will fund capital expenditure for a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat, and will also be used for general corporate purposes.
Listing is planned on the SME platform of NSE (NSE EMERGE), which will create a public trading market for the shares and enhance the company's visibility.

offer.heading: The offer and use of proceeds

beats.beat: No long-term contracts: The company relies on purchase orders rather than definitive agreements with customers and suppliers, which could lead to demand uncertainty and price volatility.
Negative cash flow in FY2017: The company reported operating cash outflow of ₹3.50 crore in FY2017, following a large inflow in FY2016. Sustained negative cash flows could strain growth investments.
Missing statutory licenses: The manufacturing facility at Plot 9-10, GIDC Waghodia lacks certain required approvals, exposing the company to potential penalties or operational disruption.

Heavy reliance on corporate promoter: The business model depends on 20 Microns Limited for marketing and sales. If this arrangement is disrupted, the company would need to build its own distribution network.
Legal proceedings: The company, its promoters, group companies, and directors are involved in legal proceedings, which could result in adverse outcomes affecting financials.
